text:
emily: heads-up — we got a customer escalation (Brightline) reporting p95 jump after the runtime v3.14 rollout to canary (~10% traffic). p95 went from ~2.3s to ~4.1s for a subset of mid-length prompts.
raj: can you paste the ticket and any sample request? which kernel/runtime change shipped with v3.14?
emily: ticket #INC-4598 (support portal). sample curl below — reproducible on our canary cohort.

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -d '{"model":"text-redwood-3","input":"summarize: 200-800 tokens","timeout":30}'

emily: traces show increased time in "kv-cache miss -> slow fetch" path. CPU on canary hosts normal, but tail latencies spike during mid-token generation (token 60-120 window).
maria: timing note — v3.14 also included the async auth-refresh optimization (opt-out for legacy tenants). any chance that's interacting? we saw auth refresh latency bumps in a1 yesterday for some tenants.
lee: dropping in — initial idea: this looks like a cold-kv path regression introduced by kernel B's cache miss handling. can we confirm whether canary uses kernel B while prod stays on kernel A?
raj: confirmed: canary = kernel-B, prod = kernel-A. kernel-B changed the kvcache eviction path and added a background fetch coalescer.
emily: I've got a repro script that hits canary and prod. quick numbers: canary p95 4.1s, prod p95 2.2s for same request set. p50 roughly same.
lee: plan: (1) collect flamegraphs + perf for kvcache miss segment on canary hosts, (2) run targeted A/B within canary: kernel-B with coalescer disabled, kernel-B with old eviction policy, (3) if repro holds, roll canary back or split canary traffic 50/50 to kernel-A variant.
raj: I'll instrument now. also doing a quick synthetic replay to reproduce at scale. if we can get the kvcache fetch latency distribution we'll know if the change amplified long tail or just added constant.
emily: FYI support escalated asking for ETA on mitigation. suggested immediate workaround: route Brightline traffic to v3.13 (prod path) until we have root cause. open to queuing that as short-term mitigation.
maria: +1 on targeted reroute for that tenant. ops-bot can you create a traffic-split command and mark as emergency for that tenant? we need minimal blast radius.
ops-bot: created routing override job 789: routes Brightline -> runtime v3.13 (apply in 2 min), rollback plan documented in infra-runbooks/traffic-overrides.md :thumbsup:
lee: if routing fix reduces customer impact, we still need to bisect kernel-B changes. raj, can you try toggling coalescer flag in-kernel first before rolling back entire kernel? that might be lower risk.
raj: working on a canary variant with COALESCER=false. spinning up a 3-node subset and replaying the sample load.
emily: I'll update the support ticket with the routing override and ETA. also adding sample logs and raw request IDs.
lee: capturing action items: 1) raj collect perf+flamegraphs by 2233337600, 2) raj deploy coalescer=false variant and run replay by 2233337800, 3) emily confirm routing override applied and inform Brightline, 4) if coalescer toggle fixes tail, plan patch to kernel-B; else rollback kernel-B from canary.
maria: ping me if reroute doesn't clear their p95 within 10m — we'll escalate to a full rollforward/rollback.
emily: thanks all — I'll post follow-ups here. :white_check_mark:
